newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe Meikles offer priced at Z$14 a shr.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe Meikles offer priced at Z$14 a shr.

text.p: Shares in Zimbabwe's Meikles Africa Ltd were priced at Z$14 a share on Thursday in the largest equity offering ever to be undertaken by a Zimbabwe-based firm.
The firm said that the offering of a stake in its hotels and supermarket groups to international investors had raised Z$720 million ($68 million).
The deal took place by way of a reverse takeover of cash shell Northchart Investments Ltd and will give Meikles a primary listing in Harare and a secondary listing in London.
"Trading starts tomorrow and the indications are it should begin at a premium," a Meikles spokesman said.
The firm aims to use the cash to develop its existing businesses which include the TM Supermarkets chain and the plush Meikles Hotel in the centre of Harare.
The group is also on the hunt for partners to extend its operations into other countries in central and southern Africa.

A Meikles spokesman told Reuters that the offer had been oversubscribed and given the firm a broad shareholding base of about 70 fund managers. Most investors were from Britain, but others hailed from Australia, the U.S. and Canada.
The group has its roots in Zimbabwe's 19th century colonial past and the starting up of a shop by Thomas Meikles in what was then known as southern Rhodesia.
The Meikles family still own a controlling stake in the group, but will see their shareholding diluted to about 55 percent, the spokesman said.

The offer greatly boosts foreign share ownership on the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange which stood at Z$1.2 billion before the deal. "It really is a market opening deal for Zimbabwe and we are confident it will encourage more foreign investment," the spokesman said.
